title: First regular Bourbon Street job with Bill Matthews
summary: Joined the former Papa Celestin band at the Paddock in 1960 and quit when billing slighted Bill Matthews.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Oh, okay. Do, um, uh, yeah, I had some questions about Bourbon Street and, and just working Bourbon Street in general. And, had, did you, did you work Bourbon Street at all in the?

Off and on. But the first regular job I had on, on Bourbon Street was in 19, uh, 1960. Uh-huh. I was playing with Bill Matthews Band. Uh-huh. You ever heard of Bill Matthews? Sure. Yeah. Well, see, it was originally Papa Celestan Band. Okay. And then Papa Celestan didn't want to work every night because he found out if he worked with spot jobs, he could make more. Uh-huh. So he, he left, he quit his whole band and got another band. And his band used Alvin Alcorn for trumpet. He replaced Papa Celestan. And Bill Matthews took over the band. And then, uh, Alvin left and he got Keg Noletti. Ernie Keg Noletti. Keg, yeah.

And then, uh, I don't know what happened, but they fired Keg and got me. I stayed there and, uh, and Steve Valenti, who owned the paddock, had my name outside, all over the place. And he was on, uh, big letters, Wallace Devonville, uh, said it like, and didn't put Bill's name out there. And Bill got mad. And he started giving me a hard way to go, so I quit.

So Steve said, no, you don't have to quit. I'll fire him. I said, no, no, Bill called, Bill called me up and gave me the job. And I'm not gonna, I'm not gonna take his foolishness. And then I'm not gonna take over his band.
